bottleneck.title: Two separate findings, not one — the original hypothesis was half right

finding_1_confirmed.title: gunicorn's default 'sync' worker class is a severe concurrency regression versus the dev server
finding_1_confirmed.root_cause: sync workers handle exactly one request at a time per process. 3 workers = 3 concurrent slots for the ENTIRE backend. 50 virtual users meant 38 of them queued behind those 3 slots at any moment.
finding_1_confirmed.evidence: With sync workers, even /api/auth/csrf/ (a GET that does zero DB work) degraded to 22s p95 at 50 users. Switching to --worker-class gthread --threads 20 (60 concurrent slots across 3 workers) brought that same endpoint back to single-digit milliseconds and notes CRUD back to ~1.1-1.4s (near dev-server parity) at the same load.
finding_1_confirmed.confidence: HIGH — directly isolated via a single-request timing test (2-20ms either way, ruling out per-request/network overhead) before and after the fix, not inferred.

finding_2_unresolved.title: Auth (register/login) latency vs notes CRUD, comparing dev server to tuned Docker, is noisy and NOT cleanly explained
finding_2_unresolved.observation: At 50 users, tuned-Docker auth latency (4.6s avg) was worse than the dev server's 50-user number (3.0s avg). At 100 users, tuned-Docker auth (2.7s avg) was BETTER than the dev server's 100-user number (6.1s avg). That's not a consistent trend in either direction.
finding_2_unresolved.honest_assessment: The original Phase 2 hypothesis (PBKDF2 hashing is CPU-bound and serializes under the GIL) is now uncertain — CPython's hashlib functions typically release the GIL during the underlying OpenSSL computation, which would undercut that theory. Plausible remaining contributors, NONE isolated as the confirmed cause: Neon connection-pool (PgBouncer) contention differing between environments, run-to-run variance on a shared free-tier Neon instance, or Docker Desktop's VM-based networking behaving differently under sustained concurrent connections versus the single-request test that ruled out baseline latency.
finding_2_unresolved.confidence: LOW — reported as genuinely open rather than dressed up with a plausible-sounding theory. Further isolation (e.g. testing against a local, non-shared Postgres to remove Neon as a variable) is deferred, not pursued indefinitely — see DEFERRED_TESTS.md.

bottleneck.reliability_note: Zero failed requests at every single stage tested, across both environments and all three worker configurations. The app never broke under load — only latency varied.

findings.title: ForeignKey(owner) auto-indexed by Django, FK constraint enforced by Postgres
findings.evidence: psql \d notes_note shows notes_note_owner_id_8dafc06d btree index and a real FK constraint to auth_user(id). Confirmed again under REL-03's true multi-process concurrency test.

findings.title: Test database teardown fails against Neon's pooled (PgBouncer) connection
findings.evidence: Unchanged from Phase 2 — psycopg.errors.ObjectInUse on manage.py test teardown.
findings.recommendation: Use Neon's direct (non-pooled) connection string for admin operations like migrate/test.

devops.reason: Docker + Docker Compose built and verified end-to-end this pass: multi-stage backend image (uv-managed deps, non-root user, gunicorn), multi-stage frontend image (Vite build -> nginx, reverse-proxying /api and /admin to the backend, SPA fallback routing), healthchecked startup ordering, whitenoise serving Django admin's static assets without a separate volume. Two real bugs found and fixed during this build, not hidden: (1) WORKDIR-created directory ownership meant a non-root user couldn't create staticfiles/ at runtime, (2) gunicorn's default sync worker class caused severe concurrency regression under load (see performance.bottleneck.finding_1_confirmed). CI (GitHub Actions) and CD (actual deployment) are separate, not yet done.
